boundaries.title: Real-data and matching boundaries
boundaries.subtitle: This game is a teaching simulation, not an exchange. The boundaries below are stated explicitly instead of hidden.
boundaries.intro: Accounting and risk logic are built to be verifiable, but the simulation still simplifies. Understanding the boundaries matters more than memorising conclusions.

futures.title: Futures: cash settled, no stock delivery
futures.body: Single-stock futures in this simulation settle in cash at expiry and never deliver shares. Margin, daily mark-to-market and cash settlement all move the account cash balance.
futures.detail: Real futures may be physically settled or cash settled; this simulation uses cash settlement to avoid stock inventory and delivery workflows.

options.title: Options: approximated American early assignment
options.body: Short options can be assigned early when deep in the money and close to expiry, delivering shares at the strike; this is not a full assignment-probability model.
options.detail: Real early assignment depends on dividends, rates, liquidity and counterparty behaviour. This simulation uses a deterministic rule to teach assignment risk, not to predict real assignment frequency.

history.title: Historical data: survivorship bias is present
history.body: Historical prices and company samples include only fictional companies that still exist today; delisted, bankrupt or acquired names are absent.
history.detail: Historical returns, factor backtests and “buy and hold” results can therefore be overstated. Real research needs delisted companies and survivorship-bias adjustments.

boundaries.note: These boundaries apply across stocks, ETFs, options, futures, history scenarios and challenge mode.

mode.backtestDesc: Run one strategy on the full sample and inspect metrics and trades.
mode.optimizeDesc: Search a parameter grid for the best in-sample result, then test it out of sample for overfitting.
mode.regressionDesc: Estimate factor premia, Rank IC and explanatory power (R²) with a pooled cross-sectional regression.
mode.mlDesc: Train cross-sectional models on momentum, low-vol, trend, news sentiment, sentiment change, analyst revisions, volume and money-flow factors, optionally search network architectures, then test an out-of-sample stock portfolio.

opt.overfitWarning: Out-of-sample performance is much weaker; this parameter set may be overfit. Do not deploy it directly.

opt.chartTitle: Out-of-sample equity of the best parameters

opt.disclaimer: Grid search itself raises the chance of overfitting; OOS results describe this sample only and do not guarantee future performance.
opt.gridNote: The optimiser searches the built-in grid and picks the best in-sample set for the chosen objective; focus on the OOS result.

reg.configSubtitle: Pooled cross-sectional regression; research only, the simulated account is unchanged.
reg.note: Runs a pooled OLS with an intercept on each day's factor cross-section and forward returns; features are standardised per date, so a coefficient is the average return tied to a one-standard-deviation move.
reg.tableSubtitle: Coefficients are average returns (%); IC is the mean cross-sectional Rank IC
reg.disclaimer: The regression only describes average in-sample relationships; factor premia change with the market regime and are not forecasts.

ml.configSubtitle: A cross-sectional market model that never changes the simulated account.
ml.configNote: Uses momentum, low-volatility, trend, news sentiment, sentiment change, analyst revisions, volume and money-flow features across 40 companies; labels are the top half of forward cross-sectional returns.
ml.overfitWarning: Out-of-sample accuracy or returns are weak; the model may be overfit. Do not use it for real trading.
ml.overfitClear: Out-of-sample results look acceptable, but more data and cost assumptions are still needed.
ml.tuningNote: Auto tuning carves a validation slice out of the training set; the out-of-sample test is never used for selection.
ml.modelNote: Features are standardised per cross-section; logistic regression shows weights and neural models show hidden-layer feature importance. News sentiment uses a 20-day window.
ml.chartSubtitle: Each OOS rebalance is held for the next horizon
ml.chartNote: The curve compounds equal-weight rebalance returns; trading costs and slippage are excluded.
ml.disclaimer: The model uses price-derived factors only and a limited sample; accuracy and past returns are not forecasts.
